lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is Tuesday's Town Council work session, where staff will dig into the Comprehensive Plan, get a Gondola Subcommittee update, and — most consequentially — review proposals for a third-party audit of the Town's rental housing policies, which cuts right to the heart of who can actually afford to live here. Ouray County's Planning Commission meets virtually Wednesday to work through proposed changes to the Land Use Code definitions, the kind of quiet shaping session that tends to matter more than it looks. Elsewhere around the valley, community events run the full range from an emergency preparedness talk Monday night to a Mountain Towns 2030 climate discussion Wednesday.

notable.stake: Third-party audit of rental housing policies could reshape who stays in the canyon.
Land Use Code definition changes being shaped before any public hearing stage.
